expected.insightNarrative:
Correlation Dashboard shows rating correlations by customer segment from a customer satisfaction survey. It is a single grid of nine scatter plots: three outcome ratings on the rows, Expertise Rating, Satisfaction Rating and Recommendation Rating, each from 0 to 10, against three drivers on the columns, How Easy to Buy, How Easy to Use and How Reliable, each scored 1 to 10. The filters Industry and Job Function are both set to All.

Key insights
- The largest response groups are all customers of 2+ years: male respondents in Accounting working in Finance (59 records), Sales (45), Other (38) and Marketing (36), and female respondents in Construction working in Finance (34).
- In every plot the trend lines slope upward: the easier a product is to buy and to use, and the more reliable it is, the higher the expertise, satisfaction and recommendation ratings.
- Customers of 2+ years sit highest and their trend lines start higher; customers of 1 year or less start lowest on satisfaction and recommendation.

Correlation
Each dot is a group of survey responses, sized by the number of records (from 1 to 59) and coloured by length of being a customer: 1 year or less, 1+ to 2 years, and 2+ years. A dashed trend line is drawn per customer-length group in each plot. The responses cluster in the upper right of every plot, with driver scores of roughly 6 to 10 matching outcome ratings of roughly 6 to 10, and all trend lines slope upward: the easier a product is to buy and use and the more reliable it is, the higher the expertise, satisfaction and recommendation ratings. Customers of 2+ years (blue) sit highest and their trend lines start higher, while the newest customers (olive) start lowest on the satisfaction and recommendation rows.
